name: LostStolenDevice
description: A case template for investigating and managing incidents involving lost or stolen endpoints, including laptops, mobile devices, tablets, removable media, or other hardware containing or providing access to organizational data. Covers device classification, encryption and MDM status verification, remote wipe, data exposure assessment, regulatory notification obligations under HIPAA and applicable US state laws, and recovery or replacement.
author: Zachary Carter
summary:
## Incident Report — [CASE TITLE]

## Executive Summary

**[Provide a high-level, non-technical summary suitable for senior leadership and stakeholders. Describe the device type, the circumstances of loss or theft, the encryption and MDM status of the device, the estimated scope of data exposure, key findings, and current response status. Typically one to three paragraphs.]**

## Scope of Investigation

**[Define the boundaries of this investigation. Identify the device, the user, the data that may have been accessible on or through the device, and any limitations on the investigation — such as inability to confirm encryption status or absence of MDM enrollment.]**

## Data Exposure Assessment

**[Summarise the data exposure assessment. Document what data was stored on the device, accessible through the device, or potentially exposed as a result of the loss or theft. Distinguish between confirmed encryption (data likely protected), unconfirmed encryption (data potentially exposed), and confirmed lack of encryption (data exposed). Identify regulatory classification of data at risk.]**

**Data exposure risk:** <!-- High — unencrypted / Medium — encryption status unknown / Low — encryption confirmed -->

**Regulatory notification triggered:** <!-- Yes / No / Under assessment -->

| Data Type | Storage Location | Regulatory Classification | Exposure Risk |
|-----------|-----------------|--------------------------|---------------|
| | On-device / Cloud / VPN-accessible | HIPAA / CCPA / PCI-DSS / Other / None | High / Medium / Low |

---

## Remediation & Recommendations

**[Prioritised remediation actions.]**

### Immediate Actions

| # | Action | Owner | Priority | Due |
|---|--------|-------|----------|-----|
| 1 | Initiate remote wipe or lock via MDM if device is enrolled and reachable | | Critical | |
| 2 | Revoke device certificates, VPN credentials, and SSO sessions associated with the device | | Critical | |
| 3 | Reset the user account password and enforce MFA re-enrollment | | Critical | |
| 4 | Confirm device encryption status through MDM, Intune, JAMF, or configuration records | | Critical | |
| 5 | Assess data stored on or accessible through the device and determine notification obligations | | High | |
| 6 | Report theft to law enforcement if applicable and obtain a police report number | | High | |
| 7 | Notify cyber insurer if device value or data exposure triggers policy obligations | | Medium | |

### Strategic Improvements

| # | Recommendation | Category | Priority |
|---|---------------|----------|----------|
| 1 | Enforce full-disk encryption on all managed endpoints — validate compliance via MDM | Endpoint | High |
| 2 | Ensure all endpoints are enrolled in MDM with remote wipe capability before deployment | Endpoint | High |
| 3 | Enforce MFA on all accounts accessible from managed devices | Identity | High |
| 4 | Implement DLP controls to restrict sensitive data storage on endpoints | Data | Medium |
| 5 | Enforce screen lock with PIN / biometric and automatic lock timeout on all mobile devices | Endpoint | Medium |
| 6 | Conduct periodic device inventory audits to identify unenrolled or unencrypted assets | Governance | Medium |

---

## Conclusion

**[Closing summary reinforcing key findings, data exposure determination, notification obligations triggered, and the path forward.]**

tasks.title: Validate and classify the device loss or theft
tasks.description: Confirm that a device has been lost or stolen. Classify the incident — lost (misplaced, no evidence of theft), stolen (confirmed or suspected intentional theft), or recovered. Document the device type, make, model, serial number, asset tag, and assigned user. Determine whether the device was a managed organizational asset, a personal device with organizational access (BYOD), or removable media.

tasks.title: Confirm device encryption and MDM enrollment status
tasks.description: Determine whether the device has full-disk encryption enabled. Confirm MDM enrollment status and retrieve device configuration records. Check MDM compliance history for encryption policy compliance. Document last known encryption status, OS version, and patch level. This is the single most important technical determination for assessing data exposure risk and regulatory notification obligations.

tasks.title: Initiate remote wipe or lock
tasks.description: If the device is enrolled in MDM and reachable, immediately initiate a remote wipe or lock. Document the wipe command issued, the time issued, and whether the wipe was confirmed as completed. If the device is not MDM-enrolled or is unreachable, document the inability to remote wipe and escalate the data exposure risk accordingly.

tasks.title: Revoke device access and credentials
tasks.description: Revoke all access associated with the device — VPN certificates, device certificates, MDM enrollment, SSO sessions, and any application sessions initiated from the device. Reset the user account password. Enforce MFA re-enrollment. Disable or revoke any API keys, tokens, or SSH keys stored on or accessible through the device.

tasks.title: Assess data stored on and accessible through the device
tasks.description: Determine what data was stored locally on the device, what data was accessible via applications, cloud sync, or VPN from the device, and whether any sensitive data was cached or downloaded. Review device configuration, installed applications, cloud sync settings, and user role to estimate data exposure scope. Identify regulatory classification of data at risk.

tasks.title: Determine HIPAA and US state privacy law notification obligations
tasks.description: Based on the device encryption status and the data accessible on or through the device, determine whether HIPAA breach notification or US state privacy law notification obligations are triggered. If encryption is confirmed and the encryption key was not also compromised, HIPAA Safe Harbor may apply. Document the legal analysis and engage legal counsel.

tasks.title: Report theft to law enforcement if applicable
tasks.description: If the device was stolen, report the theft to local law enforcement. Obtain a police report number for insurance, legal, and regulatory purposes. Provide the device serial number, asset tag, and relevant details. Document all law enforcement interactions.

tasks.title: Notify cyber insurer and assess financial impact
tasks.description: Determine whether the device loss or theft triggers cyber insurance notification obligations. Assess financial impact — device replacement cost, potential regulatory fine exposure, and breach notification costs. Notify the insurer if required.

tasks.title: Assess external reporting and notification obligations
tasks.description: Based on the data exposure assessment, determine whether and to whom notifications must be sent — HHS OCR (HIPAA), state attorneys general, affected individuals, customers, or partners. Document notification decisions, obligations, and timelines.

tasks.title: Provision replacement device and restore access
tasks.description: Issue a replacement device to the affected user with full encryption, MDM enrollment, and security controls applied before use. Restore appropriate application access and credentials. Confirm the user has received awareness guidance on device security.

tasks.title: Conduct lessons learned and close case
tasks.description: Document the circumstances of loss or theft, encryption and MDM status at time of incident, data exposure determination, notification decisions, and improvement opportunities. Confirm all required notifications are resolved and closure criteria are met.
